causes.text: In February 2025 Shell reported that its fourth-quarter 2024 revenue fell from $80.1 billion to $66.8 billion, missing expectations and highlighting weaker margins in its gas and chemicals divisions.

source_info.title: Big Oil's Showdown: How Shell, Chevron & ExxonMobil Balance Big Profits with Net Zero?

effects.text: On April 11 2025 UBS downgraded BP and criticised the performance of its gas division; BP's share price fell about 2% in response.

source_info.title: BP downgraded at UBS, as company seen weaker than peers in recession

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Shell's disappointing fourth-quarter results highlighted weakness in integrated oil companies, signalling softer demand and margin pressures across the sector.
The poor showing at Shell led analysts to reassess the outlook for peers such as BP, prompting UBS to downgrade BP and cite underperformance in its gas business.
Following the downgrade, investors sold BP shares, causing the stock to fall about 2% on the day.

rationale: Shell's weak results served as a bellwether for the oil majors, leading analysts to lower expectations for BP. The UBS downgrade amplified negative sentiment and drove BP's share price lower.
counterfactual_analysis: If Shell had reported strong results, investor confidence in integrated oil companies might have remained intact and BP may have avoided or mitigated the downgrade-induced share decline.

adversarial_confounders.text: Fluctuating natural gas prices affecting BP's own earnings
adversarial_confounders.impact: Could influence both cause and effect by altering market perceptions.

details.commentary: Weak results at Shell highlighted margin and earnings pressure in key gas and chemicals markets across the sector. Those disappointments heightened investor scrutiny of peers such as BP, making them more responsive to analyst downgrades and criticism of underperforming divisions.
